errors: log|a| = log 0.3892 = 9.590173, but Gauss writes 9.59015 (overwritten digit). The discrepancy is 2 units in the 5th place, perhaps from a slightly different working value of a.

log|b| = log 0.1592 = 9.201943, but Gauss writes 9.20205, which corresponds to 0.15924. The discrepancy is about 1 unit in the 4th place. It propagates to bb = 0.02536 (true 0.025345) and bbB = 0.3730 (true 0.3728). The effect on the final axis direction is negligible.
log|G−B| = log 0.4341 = 9.637591, written 9.63757. This is a slip of 2 units in the 5th place and is negligible.
Minor rounding: aaA true 4.0874 vs 4.0869, and ccC true ≈151.680 vs 151.6759. These are consequences of 5-place logs and inputs. They do not affect the lower (eigenvector) block.
The number read as 9.99951 must be 9.99981 (log cos 1°40'46''). Only 9.99981 gives the written final value 0.02053; 9.99951 would give 0.02083. So it is a misreading, not Gauss's error.
The quotient 28.260 = (aaA+bbB+ccC−2abc)/(aa+bb+cc) is not any root of the cubic. Its role is unexplained on the page; no error can be asserted.

results.what: Eigenvector of a symmetric 3×3 matrix [[A,c,b],[c,B,a],[b,a,C]] for eigenvalue G, with components proportional to 1/(a(G−A)+bc), 1/(b(G−B)+ac), 1/(c(G−C)+ab), normalized. Here applied numerically.
results.modern_name: Eigenvector via adjugate/cofactors of (G·I − M); principal axes of a ternary quadratic form / quadric
results.usually_credited_to: Principal-axis theory: Euler, Lagrange (1773), Cauchy (1829); explicit cofactor formulas are classical 19th-century material

results.what: Normalization of a vector given by logarithms via two auxiliary angles (tan φ = ratio, divide by cos φ), with Gaussian addition logarithms for sums
results.modern_name: Logarithmic computation of a Euclidean norm with auxiliary angles; Gaussian (addition) logarithms
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical computing practice; addition logarithms associated with Leonelli/Gauss (Gauss's table 1812)

results.what: Numerical coefficients of the characteristic cubic: Σaa, ΣaaA, 2abc; and the root G = 14.2751 of det(G·I−M) = 0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful numerical example of a closed-form principal-axis (3×3 symmetric eigenvector) computation done with logarithms. It is competent and correct to 5 places. The underlying theory (cofactor eigenvectors, α² = cofactor/f'(G)) is classical around 1809 and later standard. It is a nice unpublished worked example but not a new result.

checkable.asserts: G=14.2751 is (to ~1e-5) a root of the characteristic cubic det(G*I-M)
the cubic used corresponds to M with a on (2,3), b on (1,3), c on (1,2)
(1/𝔄,1/𝔅,1/ℭ) is an eigenvector of M for eigenvalue G
≈0.02053, the final normalization log on the page
previous-page formula α² = cofactor/f'(G) agrees with the normalized 1/𝔄 component (≈0.0322)
